  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  August 28, 2023
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:10 p.m., on Monday, August 28, 2023, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER
ABSENT:

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia,
Deputy City Manager Stover, City Clerk Myles, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of Public Works/
Utilities Ray, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director of Library LohGuan, Director of
Community Development Ho, Fire Chief Ragusa, Police Chief Kennedy, Director of Human Resources
Ko

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledged that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

READING OF ORDINANCE TITLES

Government Code Section 36934 requires that all ordinances be read in full prior to City Council taking
action on the ordinance. By listing the ordinance title on the Council agenda, Council may determine
that the title has been read.

Action Taken: By motion, determined that the titles to all ordinances which appear on this public
agenda have been read, and waive further reading.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PUBLIC HEARINGS

1.  EDWARD BYRNE MEMORIAL JUSTICE ASSISTANCE GRANT (JAG) – F2M5-41,
N2M23-98, M2M23-133

  Chief of Police KENNEDY delivered a staff report. This is the time and place set by Notice
  No. N2M23-98 for the City Council to hold a public hearing to receive community input
  concerning the use of funds received under the United States Department of Justice, Bureau
  of Justice Assistance Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) Program. The
  2023 JAG funds will be used to modernize shared work areas within the Police Department,
  such as purchasing new desks, chairs, and office equipment. The funds will also pay for
  1
8-28-23
   background investigation software and equipment/programs that will assist in the management
  and monitoring of real time crime analysis data.

  Opened/Closed Public Hearing: Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER opened the public hearing
  and, as there was no one present that wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  The Council adopted Minute Order No. M2M23-133 as follows:

  RESOLVED by the Alhambra City Council that this Council hereby authorizes
  the City Manager, or her designee, to apply for United States Department of
  Justice, Bureau of Justice Assistance -- Edward Byrne Memorial Justice
  Assistance Grant (JAG) Program funds in the amount of $13,820 and
  appropriates additional funds to enable the contract; and,

  BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED by the Alhambra City Council that this Council
  hereby ratifies the action of the City Manager in designating the Chief of Police
  or Designee as the administrator for said Grant.

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

2.  CONSIDERATION OF URGENCY ORDINANCE, ENACTED PURSUANT TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65858, EXTENDING A TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON
  THE ISSUANCE OF PERMITS OR ENTITLEMENTS FOR ANY SELF-STORAGE PROJECT
  IN THE CITY – F2M23-7, N2M23-101, O2M23-4817, M2M23-134

  City Attorney MONTES delivered a staff report. At the July 24, 2023 City Council meeting, the
  City Council adopted an urgency ordinance placing a temporary moratorium on the issuance
  of permits or entitlements for any self-storage projects in the City, exempting therefrom two
  specific projects whose entitlements were already being processed by the City (2121 Orange
  and 1146 South Meridian). The reasons for the moratorium are set forth in Ordinance No.
  O2M23-4816. Staff has not yet had a chance to further research the impacts of additional
  self-storage projects in the City, nor has staff had sufficient time to develop recommendations
  for Council’s consideration in that regard. An extension of the moratorium is necessary to
  allow staff to undertake this research and development. Consistent with the requirements of
  Government Code section 65858, an extension requires that a public hearing be conducted.
  After the public hearing, the Council can consider Ordinance No. O2M23-4817, that will extend
  the existing temporary moratorium to and through July 22, 2024. A report detailing the intended
  course of action by staff has been available in the City Clerk’s office and on the City’s website
  since August 18, 2023.

  Opened/Closed Public Hearing: Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER opened the public hearing
  and, as there was no one present that wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  The City Council:

  1.  Conducted a public hearing.
  2.  Found that the recommended action is exempt from the California Environmental
  2
8-28-23
   Quality Act ("CEQA") as set forth in the attached Urgency Ordinance (M2M23-134);
  and,

  3.  Adopted by a 4/5 vote:

  Ordinance No. O2M23-4817: An Urgency Ordinance of the City Council
  of the City of Alhambra, California, enacted pursuant to California
  Government Code Section 65858, extending a temporary moratorium on
  the issuance of permits or entitlements for any self-storage project in the
  City

  This ordinance went into effect immediately extending Ordinance No. O2M23-4816
  for a period of 10 months and 15 days, to and through July 22, 2024.

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 3-32)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 17 and 31, were considered
by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

3.  RESIDENTIAL LOW-INCOME WATER RATE ASSISTANCE PROGRAM – F2M21-49,
  M2M23-135

  The San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (SGVMWD) provides reliable supplemental
  water for the communities of Alhambra, Azusa, Monterey Park and Sierra Madre in a cost-
  effective and environmentally responsible manner. On May 24, 2021, the City entered a grant
  agreement with SGVMWD to receive $200,000.00 for assistance with delinquent water bills.
  In response, a Residential Utility Assistance Grant Program was developed by the City on
  June 3, 2021. This program offered a one-time grant up to $500 to pay delinquent water bills
  for residents with accounts 90 days or more past due. The program issued a total of
  $21,508.50 to residents for the payment of delinquent water bills, however, it closed on May
  31, 2022. Staff is proposing guidelines for the administration of a new ongoing Residential
  Low-Income Water Rate Assistance Program to utilize the remaining SGVMWD funds.
  SGVMWD was notified of the City’s intent to establish this new program. Under the new
  program, Alhambra residents will receive financial assistance in the amount of $25, which will
  be applied to the fixed portion of the bi-monthly water bill. To qualify for the program,
  applicants must be a current account holder, have a household gross annual income at or
  below 80% of the Los Angeles median income, and live at their primary residence in the City
  of Alhambra’s jurisdictional limits.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a Residential Low-Income Water Rate
  Assistance Program to provide payment support to low-income residents from the Alhambra’s
  water system charges; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M23-135)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

 4.  ACCEPT GRANT: CALIFORNIA STATE LIBRARY FOR GARDENING AND
  SUSTAINABILITY PROGRAMMING AND APPROPRIATE FUNDS – F2M23-18, M2M23-136

  The Library applied for and received a $30,000 grant from the California State Library to
  present “Let’s Grow, Alhambra! Become a Master of your Garden and Steward of Earth.” This
  gardening and sustainability-based series will include seminars from certified master
  gardeners; hands-on workshops on composting, native drought-tolerant plants, edible urban
  gardens and other specialty topics; the development of a demonstration garden; and the
  introduction of a new seed library inside the Alhambra Library.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted $30,000 from the California State Library for the
  Library Services and Technology Act Sustainability Programming Grant; appropriate revenue
  and expenditure funds in the amount of $30,000; authorized the City Manager or designee to
  sign the grant agreement, subject to final language approval by the City Manager and City
  Attorney, with the California State Library; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary
  to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-136)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  ACCEPT GRANT: CALIFORNIA STATE LIBRARY FOR ZIPBOOKS BOOK DELIVERY
  AND APPROPRIATE FUNDS – F2M23-18, M2M23-137

  The Library applied for a received a $5,171 grant from the California State Library to continue
  the purchasing of physical print and audio books to meet unique patron requests and to
  support book delivery services to home or facility bound Alhambra residents. This program
  aims to meet immediate patron requests of items the Library does not currently own and will
  enhance access for community members who have limited ability to access the Library’s
  physical building and its collection.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted $5,171 from the California State Library for the
  Zipbooks program; appropriate revenue and expenditure funds in the amount of $5,171;
  authorized the City Manager or designee to sign the grant agreement, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, with the California State Library; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-137)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  ACCEPT GRANT: OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY – SELECTIVE TRAFFIC
  ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM – F2M23-18, F2M1-77, M2M23-138

  Staff requests that the City Council authorize staff to accept the Office of Traffic Safety grant
  in the amount of $170,000. The goal of the Office of Traffic Safety is to reduce the number of
  persons killed or injured in crashes involving alcohol or other primary collision factors through
  4
8-28-23
   grant funding for local law enforcement agencies. The Alhambra Police Department intends to
  utilize the funding for the FY 2023-2024 Selective Traffic Enforcement Program to enhance
  community safety through various enforcement and education programs. Such programs and
  services will include: DUI enforcement, awareness and education programs; bicycle and
  pedestrian safety enforcement and education; participation in programs such as National Walk
  to School Day, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Winter & Summer Mobilizations,
  National Bicycle Safety Month, National Teen Driver Safety Week, National Distracted Driving
  Awareness Month, National Motorcycle Safety Month, National Child Passenger Safety Week,
  and California’s Pedestrian Safety Month.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the State of California Office of Traffic Safety
  grant in the amount of $170,000 in Fiscal Year 2023-24; authorized the Chief of Police to enter
  into a contract with the Office of Traffic Safety for grant implementation; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-138)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  ACCEPT GRANT: CALIFORNIA GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES
  UNDER THE LISTOS CALIFORNIA CERT SUPPORT GRANT PROGRAM – F2M23-18,
  M2M23-139

  The Listos California CERT Support Grant Program provides funding to support projects that
  help prepare vulnerable and underserved populations including providing Community
  Emergency Response Team (CERT) training in languages other than English and building
  capacity to respond to disasters. Staff applied to the grant program and was awarded $25,000
  for the Alhambra Fire Department to expand CERT to reach the City’s large Chinese
  population. The funds will be used for CERT training, outreach and resources in Mandarin.
  The grant performance period is June 1, 2023 through December 31, 2024.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted a grant in the amount of $25,000 from the
  California Governor’s Office of Emergency Services (Cal OES) under the Listos California
  Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) Support Grant Program; appropriated
  revenue and expenditure funds; authorized the City Manager, or designee, to execute all
  documents related to grant implementation; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-139)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

  M2M23-140

  The Spirit of Blue Foundation 501(C)(3) has selected the Alhambra Police Department to

  5
8-28-23
   alarm system. The equipment will be sourced directly from their respective manufacturers by
  Spirit of Blue and will be donated to the Alhambra Police Department.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted a gift of Police Service Dog safety equipment
  valued at $5,397.26 which is being provided by the Spirit of Blue Safety Equipment grant.
  (M2M23-140)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY

  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: 6th STREET SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT- PHASE
  II – F2M21-47, N2M23-103

  The Sewer Master Plan identified the Sixth Street sewer main between Front Street and Valley
  Boulevard as deficient in capacity and recommends replacement of the existing sewer main
  with a larger diameter sewer main. The sewer main replacement from Front Street to San
  Marino Avenue was completed in February 2022 as Phase I of the project. Phase II will include
  the Sixth Street sewer main between San Marino Avenue and Valley Boulevard. This project
  will replace approximately 1,630 feet of existing 8-inch sewer main with 15-inch sewer main.
  Plans and specifications have been prepared; staff has reviewed the plans and found them to
  be consistent with the City’s standards.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the 6th Street Sewer Main Replacement Project Phase 2 with bids due
  no later than 10:30 a.m. on September 21, 2023, and opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MAZA, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: REHABLITATION OF THE SEWER MAIN ON BEACON STREET
  – F2M23-61, N2M23-104

  The City of Alhambra Utilities Department is responsible for inspection, maintenance and
  repair of the sewer system. The Wastewater Division performs regular sewer main cleaning
  and has an ongoing program to monitor and inspect the condition of the City’s sewer collection
  system. Extreme rain events over the past few months have further degraded the condition of
  an aging sewer pipeline. On June 6, 2023, at 1010 E. Beacon Street, the sewer main became
  blocked causing sewage to overflow through a manhole into the street. City’s staff contained
  the spill and worked to clear the blocked sewer main. Lining this section of the sewer main will
  reduce the risk of future potential blockages and avoid the risk of pipe failure. Due to the sewer
  main passing through many private properties, pipe lining is the preferred method of repair.
  This section of sewer main is 6 inches in diameter and about 570 feet in length. Plans and
  specifications have been prepared; staff has reviewed the plans and found them to be
  consistent with City standards.

8-28-23
   Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Rehabilitation of the Sewer Main on Beacon Street with bids due
  no later than 10:30 a.m. on September 14, 2023, and opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY

11.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL SYSTEM CONTROL AND DATA ACQUISITION
  (SCADA) MAINTENANCE SERVICES FOR WATER AND SEWER DIVISIONS – F2M20-54,
  RFP2M23-15, C2M23-68, M2M23-141

  On May 8, 2023 the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals for
  Professional SCADA Maintenance Services for the Water and Sewer Divisions. There were
  two proposals received for the project. Staff conducted a review and evaluation of the
  responding proposals and found the proposal from SCADA Integration Inc. was the best suited
  for the City’s SCADA needs.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract, subject to final language approval
  by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and SCADA
  Integration Inc. for the Professional Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition Integration
  (SCADA) maintenance for the Water and Sewer Divisions, in an amount not to exceed
  $92,000; for the fiscal year 2023-2024 with an option for two one-year periods, and authorized
  the City Manager to execute the extensions if the services are satisfactory; and, directed staff
  to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-141)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY

12.  AWARD CONTRACT: POLICE DEPARTMENT SERVER ROOM HVAC UPGRADE –
  F2M23-51, N2M23-60, C2M23-67, M2M23-142

  On May 22, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Police Department Server Room HVAC Upgrade. Following City

  bid boards. Bids were opened by the City Clerk on July 13, 2023. A total of three bids were
  submitted ranging from $118,000.00 to $130,047.00. The lowest qualified bid was submitted
  by Pardess Air Inc. in the amount of $118,000.00. Staff has reviewed the bid submitted by
  Pardess Air Inc., and found it to be in full compliance and conformance with the project
  specifications.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Pardess Air Inc. in the amount of $118,000 for the Police

  7
8-28-23
   Department Server Room HVAC Upgrade Project; and, directed staff to undertake the steps

13.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: CITY ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR FY 2022-2023 – F2M2-
  57, C2M2-46, M2M23-143

  Transtech Engineers provides City Engineering Services to the Public Works Department on
  an as needed basis. The original contract for engineering services plan review is $200,000.00
  in the current Fiscal Year. Transtech invoices the City on an hourly basis, depending on the
  type and amount of work performed. Due to the increased amount of Accessory Dwelling Unit
  plan checks during Fiscal Year 2022-2023, Transtech work costs exceeded the contract
  amount by $51,774.50. The costs of the additional work are offset by project and plan check
  revenues collected. This amendment covers additional work performed specifically in Fiscal
  Year 2022-2023.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved an amendment to the Agreement with Transtech
  Engineers for Fiscal Year 2022-2023 for an additional $51,774.50; direct the Director of
  Finance appropriate additional funding in the amount of $43,377.10, since $8,397.40 is
  available in the fund balance; increase the Purchase Order by $51,774.50 to cover the cost of
  the additional work; authorized the City Manager to sign the Amendment on behalf of the City
  Council; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M23-143)

15.  AWARD CONTRACT: REPLACEMENT OF ALHAMBRA  POOLS  MECHANICAL
  EQUIPMENT – F2M23-31, N2M23-32, C2M23-69, M2M23-145

  On March 13, 2023, the City Council authorized the circulation of a Request for Notice Inviting
  Bids (N2M23-32) for the Replacement of Alhambra Pools Mechanical Equipment. On March
  22, 2023, staff held a job walk and four pool contractors attended. On March 30, 2023, bids
  were due; however, no bids were received by the City Clerk by the advertised date and time.
  In accordance with Article XIX, Section 135 of the City’s Charter, staff contacted a pool
  mechanical contractor to obtain a proposal to complete the project. A proposal was submitted
  by AquaSource Commercial Pool Systems in the amount of $971,894. The City works with
  Aquasource on maintenance and repairs of our pool equipment and has for many years,
  therefore, staff recommends awarding this project to Aquasource Commercial Pool Systems.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by

  allowable per Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3). On June 23, 2023, Sourcewell opened bids for
  procuring sports lighting with related supplies and services and awarded contract 041123-MSL

17.  APPROVE AN APPROPRIATION TRANSFER FOR A TEMPORARY PAW-PUP DOG PARK
  AT THE NORTHEAST PORTION OF THE ALMANSOR/CORTO UPPER PARKING LOT –
  F2M11-36, F2M18-35, M2M23-147

  At the July 25, 2022, City Council Meeting, to address Strategic Plan Item No. 9, staff identified
  four site locations for a potential dog park. Following Council discussions, staff received
  direction to pursue a dog park location at Almansor/Corto St. Staff is requesting an
  appropriation transfer of $48,998.50 to erect a temporary dog park to further assess the need
  and level of use for a dog park under a two-month study cycle. The Paw-Pup Dog Park will
  operate from dawn to dusk from September 5, 2023 through November 5, 2023. The Paw-
  Pup Dog Park will be funded with reallocated ARPA funds from a project that has not been
  initiated. This request does not impact the funding currently available under ARPA for the
  permanent dog park.

  Public Comment:

  1) Lola Armendariz asked for specific hours for the Paw-Pup Dog Park, inquired why there is
  a need for a temporary dog park, and discussed several concerns with the dog park.

  2) Shirley Tatsuno, 1408 S. Fifth St. Apt. C, inquired if dog bags will be available at the park,
  inquired if there will be shade for people,

31.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE UPDATING CHAPTER 7.04,
  SECTION 7.04.030(B), OF THE ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE BY DELETING
  LANGUAGE PERTAINING TO THE NUMBER OF RESIDENTIAL DOGS AND CATS AND
  INCORPORATING BY REFERENCE THE HIGHER LIMITS FOR RESIDENTIAL DOGS AND
  CATS ALLOWED BY THE COUNTY – F2M15-49, F2M23-7, O2M23-4814

  At the May 8, 2023 City Council meeting, Mayor Andrade-Stadler requested staff research the
  number of permittable dogs and cats per residence. Currently, Alhambra residents are
  permitted to have two dogs and four cats, per Municipal Code Section 7.04.030. The City of
  Alhambra, however, partners with the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and
  Control under a City-County Municipal Services Agreement for various animal control
  functions. The limitations under the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and
  Control Title 10 - Animals, Section 10.20.038 – Residential Dogs and Cats – Limitations specify
  the following: “A. Dogs. It is unlawful to keep more than four dogs at any residence without an
  animal facility license. Each dog must be licensed. For purposes of this section, a service dog
  licensed under Section 10.20.090 and serving a person who is disabled within the meaning of
  Government Code section 12926 subsection (i) or (j) is not counted toward the number of dogs
  kept or maintained. B. Cats. It is unlawful to keep more than five cats at any residence without
  an animal facility license. Each cat must be licensed and kept primarily indoors.” Based on the
  City’s intent to align residential cat and dog limitations with the County’s Animal Code
  Ordinance (ACO), staff is recommending striking those provisions (Section 7.040.030 (B))
  currently in the City’s Municipal Code and incorporating by reference the County’s limits of
  five cats and four dogs.
